Subject: Air-gapped update handshake: operator activation, signing, and network gating

Tom / Elena —

Thanks for agreeing to the review today. Goal: confirm the end-to-end acceptance and activation flow for air-gapped updates at Acme "sterile" sites, with a focus on:
- manifest generation and signature process (offline signer operator flow)
- courier and chain-of-custody handoff (labels + acceptance window)
- local network gating and operator activation (post-install checks)

I attached a draft operator playbook (operator-playbook-v1.3.pdf) and the manifest template. Please review the acceptance checklist on pages 4–6 and call out anything missing for your compliance team.

Proposed timeline:
- Review comments by EOD Wed (6/2)
- Small dry-run with Secure Transit on Fri (6/4)
- Formal activation window week of 6/14 if all green

Action items for today:
1) Elena — confirm signer cert rotation cadence and whether Cobalt will provide an HSM-backed signing token or an offline PKI bundle.
2) Tom — confirm courier SLA and whether your on-site operator can accept signed manifests outside normal business hours.
3) Marissa — note any procurement constraints for courier selection and insurance.

Thanks — looking to lock the acceptance gates so rollout doesn't get stuck in legal/compliance later.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: operator-playbook-v1.3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
From: elena.park@cobalt-systems.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, tom.reynolds@acme-industries.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-01T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped update handshake: operator activation, signing, and network gating

Diego, Tom —

Thanks for the clear agenda. Quick answers up front:
- Signing: Cobalt will provide an offline signer appliance (FIPS-140-2 level HSM in an air-gapped mode) that generates a detached PKCS#7 signature over the artifact manifest. The signer appliance will not be networked; we will export the signed manifest onto an encrypted USB token that is handed to courier.
- Rotation: recommended signer rotation every 12 months for production; emergency rotation procedure requires two-person operator ceremony (operator + Cobalt security engineer) and new cert issuance.
- Certificate proof: we will include a vendor-signer-certificate.pem in the distribution and publish the cert fingerprint in the manifest header.

A few open items we want to confirm:
1) Manifest format: please confirm you will accept the manifest that includes SHA256 checksums for each image artifact plus the operator-installation script checksum. We included an example in our notes.
2) Handover label: we need the courier to capture final delivery timestamp and operator badge ID (physical ID). Is Acme OK to require operator to sign the courier handheld?

We'll be on the call later today. I've attached the small signed-manifest-SHA256.txt example for your reference.

— Elena Park
Elena Park, Principal Security Engineer
Cobalt Systems

Attachment: signed-manifest-SHA256.txt (text, 2KB)
From: tom.reynolds@acme-industries.com

Subject: Re: Air-gapped update handshake: operator activation, signing, and network gating

Diego —

We reviewed the playbook internally. A few notes from the Acme ops side:
- On-site operators are available for 24x7 acceptance windows, but we require courier handoff to include operator badge + 2-factor physical confirmation (badge + operator ID printed on the manifest).
- Insurance: Secure Transit needs to include 'signed-for' value on the bill of lading for high-risk sites (we'll email you the preferred phrasing).
- Network gating: our network team will perform a pre-activation isolation test (verify no egress) and then will enable a one-time local admin approval token for the operator to begin activation. Token expires in 15 minutes.

Open question: our legal team prefers that the signed manifest include an explicit "operator acceptance" placeholder that the local operator will complete (printed name, badge#, and timestamp). Can Redwood produce a printable manifest variant? If so, we can streamline acceptance.

— Tom
Tom Reynolds
Operations Manager, Acme Industrial Controls

Attachment: courier-requirements.pdf (PDF)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com

Date: 2026-06-03T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped update handshake: operator activation, signing, and network gating

All —

Technical clarifications from Redwood runtime side:
- Manifest contents: we will embed per-image SHA256 and image size, plus an overall bundle UUID and the vendor signer cert fingerprint (SHA256). The install agent will verify each artifact before writing to disk; install fails open is not allowed.
- Printable manifest: yes — we can emit a two-column printable manifest (artifact | checksum) with an "Operator acceptance" block that prints operator name, badge ID, and timestamp. We'll include a machine-readable detached signature file (PKCS#7) and a printable copy that the operator signs at handoff.
- Activation token: the install agent will accept a single-use HMAC token generated by Acme's network gating service; token TTL configurable (we recommend 15 mins for safety). Token validation happens fully local; there is no outbound call.

A couple of implementation notes for the dry-run Friday:
1) We need one target site (non-production) where operators can practice the physical manifest acceptance and token activation flow.
2) Please have Secure Transit provide a scan of their handheld acceptance capture format (CSV) so we can ingest it into our audit logs for traceability.

I'll attach a short runbook snippet to the playbook for the install agent verification flow.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Next milestone: schedule the production activation window week of 2026-06-14. Diego, please coordinate with Cobalt for certificate push and with Secure Transit for final slot.

Thanks everyone — clean dry-run. Uploading the final vendor-signer-certificate.pem to the shared drive and starting the DocuSign envelope for the courier SLA.

— Marissa Cole
